headline: CSRD Progress, EUDR Penalties, and Green Claims Ban Take Centre Stage
summary: Germany is close to finalising its CSRD transposition, which will apply to you from 2027. Meanwhile, severe national EUDR penalties are being proposed, and the EU's ban on vague green claims has entered into force, requiring immediate marketing audits.

items.title: Germany nears finalisation of CSRD transposition law
items.what: The German SPD announced that negotiations on the national CSRD transposition law are complete, paving the way for final legislative adoption.
items.meaning: As a listed brand with over 1,000 employees, you must prepare for mandatory CSRD reporting starting in financial year 2027.
items.action: Ensure your sustainability data collection systems are ready for the upcoming German requirements.

sources.title: CSRD-Umsetzungsgesetz: SPD sieht Verhandlungen als abgeschlossen

items.title: Severe national EUDR penalties proposed alongside customs updates
items.what: Germany and Ireland proposed severe penalties for EUDR breaches, including €10m fines and prison sentences. The EU also updated customs codes.
items.meaning: If your power tools contain rubber, wood, or paper packaging, compliance before the December deadline is critical to avoid severe penalties.
items.action: Map supply chains for rubber and packaging with Chinese suppliers immediately.

sources.title: German EUDR draft sets turnover-linked fines and criminal penalties for serious breaches
Germany’s EUDR Bill Seeks Up to Ten Years in Prison for Breaches
Companies that fail to meet Ireland's Deforestation Regulations could be fined up to 10 million euros
EU updates EUDR customs codes and Information System guidance ahead of December application

items.title: EU ban on vague green claims enters into force
items.what: The EU ban on vague environmental claims has officially entered into force, targeting unsubstantiated greenwashing in consumer marketing.
items.meaning: Your consumer-facing brand must ensure all environmental claims on power tools and packaging are backed by verified evidence.
items.action: Audit product packaging and marketing materials to remove unverified claims.

sources.title: Goodbye greenwashing? EU ban on vague claims comes into force

items.title: Industry groups oppose proposed downstream CBAM extensions
items.what: Automotive and supplier associations issued joint statements calling for workable rules and opposing proposed downstream extensions of CBAM to finished products.
items.meaning: Although you currently import finished goods exempt from CBAM, downstream extensions could bring your imported power tools into scope.
items.action: Monitor policy debates regarding downstream CBAM extensions closely.

sources.title: Joint statement on the proposed downstream extension of the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM)
CLEPA joins call for workable CBAM rules that protect the entire automotive value chain
sources.origin: CLEPA | European Association of Automotive Suppliers

items.title: First digital battery passports emerge ahead of EU deadlines
items.what: An e-bike brand launched a digital battery passport, demonstrating early market readiness for upcoming EU battery regulation requirements.
items.meaning: As a brand with its own battery platform, you will face similar digital passport requirements for your power tool batteries.
items.action: Engage with your Chinese battery suppliers to develop digital passport capabilities.

sources.title: TENWAYS unveils digital passport for eBike batteries ahead of EU deadline

watch: The entry into force of the revised ESRS on 10 November 2026, which will govern your CSRD reporting.
The application of the EUDR on 30 December 2026, requiring strict supply chain tracing for wood and rubber.
The application of the new Machinery Regulation on 20 January 2027, replacing the current Machinery Directive.
